question.text: On complete combustion, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>492</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of an organic compound gave <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>792</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math> of carbon in the organic compound is (Nearest integer)

solution.text:
44 grams of CO2 contain 12 grams of carbon.

Hence, one gram of carbon dioxide contain 1244 gram of carbon.

0.792 gram of carbon dioxide contain 1244 × 0.792 gram of carbon

Percentage of carbon = Mass of carbonMass of organic compound × 100

= 1244 × 0.7920.492 ×100

= 43.90%

So, answer is 44.
